Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

damage verb and noun

also damaged, be damaged, spoil, ruin, storm damage

classical

Verg. G. 2.220: nec scabiē et salsā laedit rōbīgine ferrum
Ov. F. 6.150: frondēs laedit hiems (Lewis & Short)

laedō, laedere, laesī, laesum

verb, third conjugation

damage, harm, hurt

Lewis & Short: “to hurt by striking, wound, injure, damage”; of frost, rust and weather as of blows.

Examples

  • sī enim nihil est in parietibus aut in tēctō vitī, cētera mihi probābuntur

    for if there’s no damage in the walls or the roof, I’ll be happy with the restCic. Fam. 9.15.5

  • cernis ut ignāvum corrumpant ōtia corpus, ut capiant vitium, nī moveantur, aquae

    you see how idleness spoils a lazy body, as water goes bad if it doesn’t moveOv. Pont. 1.5.5–6

  • onerāriās, quae ad ancorās erant dēligātae, tempestās adflīctābat

    the storm was battering the transports that were riding at anchorCaes. BG 4.29.2

Other words

  • vitium, vitiī n. — damage, a defect (in a building or a thing)

    noun, second declension · classical · Cic. Fam. 9.15.5: sī enim nihil est in parietibus aut in tēctō vitī; Cic. Top. 15: sī aedēs corruērunt vitiumve fēcērunt (Lewis & Short)

    To become damaged, of a building: vitium facere (Cic. Top. 15); of water going bad, vitium capere (Ov. Pont. 1.5.6).

  • corrumpō, corrumpere, corrūpī, corruptum — spoil, ruin (food, goods, crops)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 3.2: nē corrumpātur; Plaut. Ps. 892: corrumpitur jam cēna

  • damnum, damnī n. — harm, loss suffered

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 3.3: damnī nihil erit ex tempestāte

    The damage as what it costs the owner (see loss).

  • afflīctō, afflīctāre, afflīctāvī, afflīctātum — batter, knock about (of storms)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Caes. BG 4.29.2: tempestās adflīctābat

See also broken, hurt yourself, loss.

SourcesLewis & Short: laedo · Lewis & Short: vitium · Lewis & Short: corrumpo · Lewis & Short: damnum · Lewis & Short: afflicto
